title: The Gilding of New Troy
descriptionHtml:
'New Troy' refers to the city of London. Here are some words found on the internet:
"Aeneas was a lieutenant of Hector in the Trojan War, and when the city was destroyed (after deployment of the Trojan Horse) he fled to Italy where the settlement he founded was later to become Rome. His grandson was named Brutus. The mother of Brutus died in childbirth and he accidentally killed his father in a hunting accident, so was banished for being 'unlucky'. He then set off in search of new lands. The defeated Trojans adopted him as their leader and they became collectively known as 'Britons'. They headed past the ‘Pillars of Hercules’ (the Straits of Gibraltar), and reached Albion. Albion was inhabited by an island race of giants. Corineus, a warrior of great repute, wrestled with the giant race's leader Gogmagog, before hurling him over the cliffs of Plymouth Hoe. Brutus and his Britons sailed up the Thames and founded a new city 'Troia Nova’."
The account above is not widely believed.
As you cannot have failed to notice, 52% of the people who voted in the UK's referendum on membership of the European Union decided that England was better off going it alone, somewhat like a spoilt, sulking child at a party. Whatever you may think of this 'decision', perhaps this is the time to enjoy a picture of London's financial district being simultaneously flooded and burnt down. Screen printed and hot-foiled with gold foil. Perhaps our overseas visitors might like to consider taking advantage of the low-value English 'pound' to purchase one of these artifacts?

1 colour screen print on gold anodised aluminium foil heat-pressed on 270gsm paper.
Paper Size - 380mm x 330mm
Print Size - 288mm x 215mm
From an edition of 200 prints

title: Dark Estuary
descriptionHtml:
Some of my days and some of my nights are spent slouching around an estuary in East Anglia, north of London. The ripples on a calm night are quietly hypnotic. There’s not much more to say.

‘Dark Estuary’ is the title of a book by ‘BB’, the pen-name of Denys Watkins-Pitchford, written in 1953.

3 colour screen print
Paper size 440mm x 600mm
Print size 360mm x 495mm
Printed on acid-free archival 300gsm somerset satin
From an edition of 120 prints

title: Holding Hands
descriptionHtml:
This print is based on a drawing made for a book called ABC, which was a limited edition title produced by MA students from The London College of Communication; it was intended to raise money for, and awareness of, The British Red Cross. My letter was H. The drawing itself was snapped from an exhibition in 2013. The surface of the moon, printed in silver, is from a NASA photograph of the other, 'dark' side of the moon. 

3 colour screen print
Paper size: 450mm x 600mm

Printed on acid-free archival 300gsm somerset satin 
From an edition of 122 prints

title: Wait Here We Will Come For You
descriptionHtml:
I made the drawing on which this print is based over about four months, using very thin pens on a large piece of paper. The title that it ended up with - 'wait here, we will come for you' - is rather ambiguous and could be interpreted in a number of ways. I'm not sure if it shows a search party or a line of hunters. It's up to you, really. It probably depends on what kind of outlook you have.

3 colour screen print
Paper size: 580mm x 460mm
Print size: 500mm x 360mm
From an edition of 122 prints

title: Lost at Sea
descriptionHtml:
This is a reflection. It is how things are. There is land, but it is far and the waves are many and tumultuous. There is moonlight, but there are storm clouds gathering. Lost, and at sea.
